hotspots.label: wheel
hotspots.title: Aluminum wheels
hotspots.description: The perseverance Rover has six aluminum wheels

hotspots.label: drill
hotspots.title: Coring Drill
hotspots.description: The perseverance Rover uses the core drill to extract samples from the Martian surface

hotspots.label: navcam
hotspots.title: Engineering Camera
hotspots.description: The engineering navigation cameras (NVACAM) capture images of the terrain which can be used to help with rover navigation.

hotspots.label: supercam
hotspots.title: Laser micro-imager (SUPERCAM)
hotspots.description: The laser micro-imager (SUPERCAM) is a remote-sensing instrument used for spectral analyses.

hotspots.label: moxie
hotspots.title: MOXIE Oxygen producer
hotspots.description: MOXIE has produce oxygen from carbon dioxide in the Martian atmosphere using solid oxide electrolysis.

hotspots.label: powerSupply
hotspots.title: Plutonium-based power supply
hotspots.description: The radioisotope thermoelectric generator (RTG) powers the rover using the heat of plutonium's radioactive decay.

hotspots.label: rimfax
hotspots.title: Radar Imager for Mars' subsurface experiment (RIMFAX)
hotspots.description: RIMFAX is a ground-penetrating radar designed to help scientists see below the martian surface. It is the first radar of its kind to reside on the ground of the Red Planet and may penetrate to depths over 30 feet (10 meters).

hotspots.label: arm
hotspots.title: Robotic arm
hotspots.description: The 7-foot robotic arm has flexibility through three joints with five degrees of freedom.

hotspots.label: suspension
hotspots.title: Suspension
hotspots.description: The "rocker-bogie" suspension system helps the rover drive over the varied Martian terrain.

hotspots.label: differential
hotspots.title: Differential
hotspots.description: A pivot in the top deck's center connects it to the left and right rockers and the rover body.
